title: Pointed affine etale quasi-splitting of a flat locally quasi-finite groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $U$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $s,t:R\to U$ are separated (their diagonals are closed immersions [def-weil-proper-morphism]), flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. For every point $u\in U$ there exist an affine $S$-scheme $W$, an etale morphism $g:W\to U$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $w\in W$ with $g(w)=u$ and induced residue-field map $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(w)$ an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $R_W=W\times_{g,U,s}R\times_{t,U,g}W$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with its restricted groupoid on $W$. Its projections $s_W,t_W:R_W\to W$ are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite. There is an open subscheme $P\subseteq R_W$ [def-weil-open-immersion] containing the entire unit section and closed under inverse and composition, such that $(W,P,s_W|_P,t_W|_P,e_W,i_W|_P,c_W|_{P\times_WP})$ is a groupoid and both $P\to W$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. All objects may be taken within the chosen site bound.

source.place: Tag 04S0 (lemma-quasi-splitting-affine-scheme), with Situation situation-quasi-splitting and Tag 04RK (definition-split-at-point), quasi-splitting clause (3). The restricted projections retain their properties by etale base change and composition; the finite projections of the open subgroupoid are flat and locally of finite presentation, hence finite locally free.

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$. Apply [lem-sfb-section-marked-finite-parts-scheme] to $f=s:R\to U$ and its section $e$. It gives a separated etale $g_0:M\to U$, a point $m$ over $u$ with the prescribed residue-field isomorphism, and the universal finite clopen $Q\subseteq R\times_{s,U,g_0}M$. The point clause applies since $s$ is locally quasi-finite, in particular quasi-finite at $e(u)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], $s,t$ are locally of finite type, so [lem-sfb-universal-finite-parts-groupoid] gives the groupoid $(M,Q)$, its morphism to $(U,R)$, and finite projections $s_Q,t_Q$.

source.place: Tags 04RI, 04RR, 04RU and 04RW: parameter scheme, chosen point and finite-part groupoid

proof.text: Put $E=R\times_{s,U,g_0}M$ and $H=M\times_{g_0,U,s}R\times_{t,U,g_0}M$. The map $H\to E$ forgetting the target lift is a base change of the separated etale map $g_0$, hence separated and etale [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The groupoid morphism of step 1 gives $j:Q\to H$ over the inclusion $Q\subseteq E$. Its graph $Q\to H\times_EQ$ is a section of a separated etale morphism, hence a clopen immersion [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. The projection $H\times_EQ\to H$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Composing these two open immersions identifies $Q$ with an open subscheme $P_0\subseteq H$; composition is an open immersion because the maps identify source schemes with open subschemes with restricted structure sheaves [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since $j$ respects all operations, $P_0$ is a subgroupoid on all objects $M$, containing the entire unit section.

source.place: Tag 04RW, first paragraph: open immersion of the finite-part groupoid into the restricted relation

proof.text: The map $H\to R$ is a composite of two base changes of $g_0$, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] to the squares over $s$ and $t$, with horizontal etale maps $H\to R$ and $M\to U$: both projections $H\to M$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. They are also locally quasi-finite: each is the composite of a base change of $s$ or $t$ and a base change of $g_0$; etale maps are unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally quasi-finite [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points], and use [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change, lem-a1-scheme-lqf-composition]. Precomposition with the open immersion $P_0\to H$ preserves flatness and local finite presentation, by its etaleness and the same source-and-target lemma. Since $P_0\simeq Q$ has finite projections by step 1, [def-pc-finite-locally-free] makes both projections finite locally free.

source.place: Tags 04S0 and 04MP: restricted projection properties; finiteness applies to the open subgroupoid

proof.text: The orbit $O(m)=t_Q(s_Q^{-1}(\{m\}))$ is finite, because $s_Q$ is finite and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] gives finite fibres. The unit shows $m\in O(m)$. The morphism $g_0$ is separated and etale, hence locally quasi-finite by [def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points]. Its target $U$ is affine. Thus [lem-sfb-separated-lqf-affine-finite-set] supplies an affine open of $M$ containing $O(m)$. Applying [lem-sfb-locally-free-groupoid-invariant-affine] to the groupoid $(M,Q)$ yields an affine open $W\subseteq M$ containing $O(m)$ such that $s_Q^{-1}(W)=t_Q^{-1}(W)$. In particular $m\in W$.

source.place: Tag 04S0 via lemma-strong-splitting-affine-scheme: finite orbit and invariant affine neighborhood; affine finite-set input also Tag 07S0

proof.text: Let $P=Q\times_{s_Q,M}W$. Invariance makes this also $Q\times_{t_Q,M}W$ and the two-sided restriction $W\times_MQ\times_MW$: an arrow with one endpoint in $W$ has both endpoints in $W$. By [lem-a1-groupoid-invariant-open-restriction-degree] the operations restrict to a groupoid $(W,P)$. Both $P\to W$ are finite as base changes of $s_Q,t_Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Flatness and local finite presentation follow from the source-and-target lemma applied to the open restriction squares [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so they are finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The map $P\to R_W$ is the base change of $P_0\to H$ along $R_W\to H$, hence open [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Here the fibre-product identity follows by specifying the two endpoints in $W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its units, inverses and composition are the restricted operations, giving precisely the required open subgroupoid.

source.place: Tag 04S0 via lemma-strong-splitting-affine-scheme, final paragraph: invariant restriction preserves finite projections

proof.text: Take $g=g_0|_W$ and $w=m$ regarded as a point of $W$. This composite of an open immersion and an etale morphism is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. An open immersion induces residue-field isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], so $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(w)$ is the isomorphism from step 1 followed by an isomorphism, and $g(w)=u$. For $R_W\to W$ the argument of step 3 applies with the etale map $g$: $R_W\to R$ is etale by base change and composition, the source-and-target lemma gives flatness and local finite presentation, and the factorization into a base change of $s$ or $t$ and a base change of $g$ gives local quasi-finiteness using the cited permanence lemmas. All parameter schemes in step 1 and all subsequent fibre products and open subschemes lie in the chosen universe; passing to its fixed site skeleton is allowed by [def-weil-size-convention].
